messages:
maya: quick FYI - ran a small dedicated pool trace yesterday. attaching full nsys in prod caused measurable latency regressions. we need a lighter approach for ongoing profiling.

jonah: how bad was it? any sign KV cache behavior changed?

sara: short notes from the capture run:
- full capture (nsys full mode): median latency +10%, p95 +18%, p99 +25%
- host enqueue stalls increased; observed extra synchronization around kernel launch points
- KV hit-rate and evictions looked unchanged, but request-side queue depth grew under profiler

jonah: that syncing is the usual culprit — NVTX and full tracing break continuous batching and some kernel fusion heuristics.

kai: options to reduce impact:
- use nsys sampling mode instead of full capture
- probe windows (duty-cycle) instead of continuous capture
- offload capture metadata to a sidecar so the runtime avoids NVTX in hot path
- whitelist only a few heavy kernels to limit scope

maya: sara, what nsys flags did you run for the full capture?

sara: pasted the command:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --output=prod_full_trace
# runtime still emits NVTX markers around launches
```

sara: full mode also doubles trace size; switching to device sampling reduced size but still introduced overhead.

jonah: microbench numbers on staging-gpu3 with our bench script:
- full nsys: +45% wall time
- device sampling (1us): +6%
- duty-cycle 5s on / 60s off: +2%

kai: can you paste the bench command so i can try a sidecar prototype?

jonah: `python bench_load.py --batch-size 4 --seq-length 2048 --iters 800` with RUNTIME_NVTX toggled.

maya: ops constraint: profiling in production must have a kill-switch, automated guardrails, and be applied to a tiny canary only. proposing a "sideloaded probe" policy.

maya: proposed safe-prod probe policy (draft):
1) profiling disabled by default in prod control plane
2) enable only on a canary slice (0.5% traffic) with an explicit rollout flag
3) use sampling-mode traces with duty-cycle: probe 5s every 60s
4) sidecar receives lightweight launch markers over UDS; no NVTX in hot path
5) kernel whitelist default: [softmax, matmul, layer_norm]; dynamic add-on allowed
6) abort and rollback if median latency > baseline + 2ms OR p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.12 OR error-rate +0.2% change

sara: dynamic whitelist idea: if an unlisted kernel shows >3x relative latency during a probe window, automatically capture it for 1 extra window. add cooldown to avoid churn.

kai: agree to dynamic add, but we must cap extra kernels and add cooldown. suggested params: min-capture 10m, max-extra-kernels 2, cooldown 10m per kernel.

perf-bot: [automated] alert: runtime v2.15 increased NVTX annotations per request by ~9. See /perf/trace-diff/v2.15

jonah: sidecar sketch: runtime writes tiny records to a bounded MPSC ring buffer (kernel_id, launch_ts, seq_len, thread_id). sidecar pulls entries and drives sampling/post-process runs. avoids NVTX and keeps hot path non-blocking.

maya: memory risk on high QPS. ring buffer size must be bounded and the runtime should drop profiling baggage when full. track drop metrics in telemetry.

sara: proposed runtime config snippet for the probe:
```
profiler:
  enabled: true
  mode: sampling
  probe_ms: 5000
  off_ms: 60000
  kernel_whitelist: [softmax, matmul, layer_norm]
  max_extra_kernels: 2
  ring_buffer_entries: 32768
```

jonah: testing plan:
- reproduce microbench numbers on staging with identical flags (today)
- deploy canary (0.5%) for 24 hours with dashboards and auto-rollback rules
- monitor median/p95/p99, gpu_util, ring_buffer_fill, and S3 upload errors

maya: dashboard needs these panels:
- rolling 1m median vs baseline
- probe hit/drop rate
- ring buffer utilization and drop count
- per-kernel added latency estimate (ms)

kai: per-kernel latency estimate approach: A/B on a randomized small slice inside the canary (instrumented vs control) and compute median delta per kernel tag. noisy but ok if we aggregate over many windows.

sara: also log kernel selection id in traces — profiling can change kernel choice. capture kernel_hash and seq_len for correlation.

jonah: action items:
- sara: build sidecar prototype + runtime ring buffer hooks, open PR with flags and a README (ETA 48h)
- kai: implement dynamic whitelist and cooldown in rollout agent (ETA 72h)
- maya: create canary dashboard and rollback runbook (ETA tomorrow morning)
- jonah: run staging microbench and upload traces (ETA end of day)

maya: if canary shows small spikes, first try shrinking probe window (e.g., 2s on / 120s off) before disabling entirely.

sara: will open PR and include microbench tarball and the sidecar README.

perf-bot: [automated] created ticket #4082: 'sideloaded-probe-sampling' and attached perf logs.

alex (eng-oncall): i'll monitor canary. set me an alert to kill profiling if p99 exceeds baseline * 1.25.

maya: note: document the experiment in release notes and ops runbook so oncall/sre know expected behavior.

jonah: uploaded staging traces: s3://redwood-internal/profiler/trace_2143658700.tar.gz

sara: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/801 (draft)

maya: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the first 24h canary window.
